newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech to refile long-distance FCC bid soon.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech to refile long-distance FCC bid soon.

text.p: Ameritech Corp. expects to refile by the end of March its landmark request with regulators to enter the $80 billion long-distance phone business, the company's chairman said Wednesday.

The Chicago-based Baby Bell was forced earlier this month to yank its bid after the Federal Communications Commission said the application to offer Michigan residents long-distance service contained major inaccuracies.

Ameritech Chairman Richard Notebaert told reporters he expects the process will go "quite smoothly" the second time around. The company must first wait for Michigan regulators to formally approve a pact with AT&T Corp. showing that Ameritech has opened its Michigan network to the long-distance giant.

Under last year's telecommunications reform law, Ameritech and the other Baby Bells must show regulators they have opened their local phone monopolies to new competitors before they can offer long-distance service to local customers.
Ameritech, which first sought FCC approval Jan. 2, hopes to be the first regional Baby Bell company to do so.

Ameritech pulled its initial request after the FCC noted that Michigan had not approved the company's "interconnection" agreement with long-distance giant AT&T. Ameritech had contended state regulators had given their approval.

Notebaert declined to be specific about the company's long-distance plans after Michigan. He did note that, aside from Michigan, Ameritech has made the most progress with regulators in Wisconsin and Illinois.
In addition to Michigan, Illinois and Wisconsin, Ameritech offers local phone service in Indiana and Ohio.

Ameritech officials said that, before they can refile their Michigan bid, state regulators there must issue a formal document and order saying the company's pact with AT&T has been approved and is consistent with an arbitration accord struck between the two carriers last November.
